newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close mixed in in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close mixed in in thin trade.

text.p: Tel Aviv shares closed mixed with a positive bias on Monday in very light trade, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 0.26 percent, or 0.48 points, to 187.52 on extremely low turnover of 37.5 million shekels against 35 million on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index rose 0.32 percent to 197.51.

"Activity continues to be very low and most shares were not traded at all. Because of the low activity shares moved sharply on extremely low turnover," said Doron Tsur, head of research at Sahar Securities.

"Everything is accidental in the market and it is impossible to trade. We hope that the activity will rise towards the end of the month when companies start publishing their earnings reports," Tsur said.

The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange said in its monthly report that average daily turnover in October was the lowest in recent years. The average volume fell to 70 million shekels from an average of 110 million shekels during the first nine months of the year.

Bezeq Israel Telecom rose 2.75 percent to 814 on volume of 1.4 million shekels. A senior official at the Communications Ministry said that Britain's Cable & Wireless Plc has asked to increase its stake in Bezeq to 21 percent. C&W currently owns 10 percent of the government controlled phone monopoly.
Bank Leumi lost 0.75 percent to 360 despite news that the government is planning a secondary offering for 10 percent of the bank, probably in the first quarter of 1997.
"There is no market. Activity is low and investors are sitting on the fence. The only positive thing is that the market remains stable," said Ron Weisberg at I.B.I Investment House.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which rose 0.25 percent to 28,040 on volume of 3.9 million shekels and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which closed unchanged at 138,999 on turnover of 3.8 million shekels.

Maman Cargo Terminals and Handling surged 7.5 percent to 669 on volume of 1.5 million shekels. Traders said the share rose following large off-the-floor transactions made as part of a battle for control in the company.
